articles.title: This is not standard flooding; it is a Himalayan Tsunami: Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal
articles.summary: Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal described the recent catastrophic flooding in Nepal as a "Himalayan Tsunami," emphasizing that the disaster was unprecedented and not a typical flood. Multinational rescue teams are contending with rapidly changing terrain to access buried hydropower tunnels damaged by the event. Khanal announced that Nepal will seek legal climate compensation, arguing that the nation bears no responsibility for the climate‑driven calamity. The minister called for international accountability and support to rebuild infrastructure and address the broader impacts of climate change on the Himalayan region.

articles.title: Hundreds missing, billions in goods feared lost in Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: A severe flood in the Bhotekoshi River swept through Nepal's Rasuwa border area, leaving hundreds of traders, drivers and customs workers missing after six days. Authorities are still unable to confirm the exact number of cargo containers lost, but estimates suggest billions of rupees worth of merchandise may have been washed away. Rescue and recovery efforts are ongoing, with officials coordinating with local agencies to locate the missing and assess the economic impact on cross‑border trade. The disaster has highlighted vulnerabilities in the region's infrastructure and raised concerns over the safety of workers and the continuity of trade flows.

articles.title: Nepal seeks urgent climate finance after Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has appealed to the United Nations‑backed Global Loss and Damage Fund for immediate climate finance following the devastating Bhotekoshi River flood. Officials say the scale of destruction—affecting thousands of homes, infrastructure and livelihoods—far exceeds the country's capacity to respond, prompting urgent calls for international assistance to rebuild and enhance resilience.

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 987, nearly 4,000 still missing
articles.summary: A devastating flood in Nepal has pushed the death toll to 987, with nearly 4,000 people still missing. Search teams are retrieving bodies in Rasuwa district and downstream areas, while hundreds of workers at various hydropower construction sites remain unaccounted for. The disaster has sparked a massive rescue effort across the country, highlighting the scale of the humanitarian crisis.

articles.title: They survived the flood. Their families did not.
articles.summary: Survivors at a holding centre in Rasuwa recount the harrowing aftermath of the Bhotekoshi flood, describing desperate escapes as waters swept away relatives, homes, and entire villages. While some individuals managed to survive, many families were lost, leaving the community grappling with profound grief and the challenge of rebuilding after the disaster.

articles.title: What is the progress in the search for workers trapped in Nepal’s flooded hydropowers?
articles.summary: Rescue teams have made progress in locating tunnel entrances and have advanced hundreds of metres into several flooded hydropower projects along Nepal's Bhotekoshi‑Trishuli corridor. The search for workers trapped by the floods continues as authorities assess the extent of damage and coordinate further rescue efforts.

articles.title: Nepal Prime Minister: Bhotekoshi flood was one of region’s largest disasters
articles.summary: Prime Minister of Nepal said the Bhotekoshi flood ranks among the largest disasters in the Himalayan region, underscoring that climate‑change‑driven risks are rising for the country.

articles.title: Iran’s president says Tehran will reciprocate if US honours interim deal commitments
articles.summary: Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi warned that Tehran will only permit free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz—a crucial route for global oil—if the United States fully implements its obligations under the interim nuclear agreement. The statement underscores Tehran’s stance of reciprocal action, linking maritime freedom to U.S. compliance with the deal’s terms.

articles.title: Local governments take charge of flood relief after criticism of centralised response
articles.summary: After criticism of the central government's reliance on security agencies for flood relief, local authorities in Nepal have taken the lead. Six‑party committees have been set up in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot to coordinate the distribution of aid and resources to affected communities. The move aims to improve responsiveness, ensure equitable assistance, and address concerns that the initial response was too centralized and slow. While the shift to local management is welcomed, officials acknowledge challenges in logistics and funding as the monsoon season continues.

articles.title: After days of managing flood victims, Bharatpur Hospital returns to treating patients
articles.summary: Bharatpur Hospital in Chitwan, Nepal, has resumed regular patient care after spending several days handling the aftermath of severe flooding. The hospital managed the recovery of 321 flood victims' bodies, and over two days buried 199 of them, which relieved the strain on its morgue. With the morgue pressure eased, the facility can now focus on treating living patients again, marking a return to normal operations following the disaster.

articles.title: China and India should do more to save the Himalaya system
articles.summary: The article discusses the need for China and India to take climate action to save the Himalaya system.

articles.title: The case for transparency in Nepal flood rescue flights
articles.summary: The article argues that during recent floods in Nepal, helicopters became the sole means of rescue after roads were washed away. It criticizes politicians and media crews for occupying these aircraft, diverting them from genuine rescue operations. The piece calls for greater transparency and accountability in the allocation and use of rescue flights, urging authorities to prioritize victims over personal or political agendas.

articles.title: Prioritise psychological support for those affected by the Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: The article urges Nepalese authorities and aid agencies to expand psychological counselling services for victims of the recent Bhotekoshi flood. It stresses that mental health support should not be limited to the hardest‑hit districts, but also reach displaced families in their new locations and communities of origin. The piece highlights the long‑term trauma caused by floods and calls for coordinated efforts among government, NGOs, and health professionals to provide accessible, culturally appropriate counselling.

articles.title: Nepal steps up diplomatic push for support after floods
articles.summary: After severe floods, Nepal’s government is intensifying diplomatic outreach to secure climate‑related recovery funds, tunnel rescue teams, forensic expertise and critical equipment to aid reconstruction and disaster response.

articles.title: UN Women estimates 43,000 women and girls in Nepal need urgent flood assistance
articles.summary: UN Women estimates that 43,000 women and girls in Nepal require urgent flood assistance, part of a larger group of 157,050 women and girls in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot who have been directly or indirectly affected by recent floods. Immediate needs include food, safe drinking water, and protection services. The agency urges rapid humanitarian response to address these critical gaps and mitigate the impact on vulnerable female populations.

articles.title: 1.6 million affected by Bhotekoshi floods, says government report
articles.summary: A government situation report on the Bhotekoshi floods in Nepal says the disaster has impacted about 1.6 million people. The death toll stands at 1,050 with nearly 4,000 still missing. Over 21,000 security personnel are engaged in a massive rescue effort, supported by international teams, as authorities continue to respond to the widespread damage.

articles.title: Drones take on a new role in Nepal’s disaster response—from delivering food to carrying bodies
articles.summary: After being used mainly by international rescue teams during the 2015 earthquake, Nepal has developed its own drone expertise that is now integral to domestic disaster response. Local agencies employ drones to deliver food, medicine and other supplies, conduct aerial searches for survivors, and even transport bodies from inaccessible zones, reducing risk to rescuers and speeding up operations. The expanding role of unmanned aerial vehicles marks a significant shift in how the country manages emergencies, highlighting both technological advancement and improved coordination among authorities and humanitarian groups.

articles.title: Authorities scramble for alternatives after Krishnabhir road cave-in
articles.summary: A 70‑metre section of the Krishnabhir road has collapsed into the Trishuli River, with an additional 120 metres severely cracked, prompting Nepalese authorities to urgently seek alternative routes and solutions. The incident has disrupted transport and raised concerns about infrastructure safety in the region, leading officials to coordinate emergency response and assess repair options.

articles.title: Family performs funeral rites after Bhotekoshi flood victim’s body goes missing
articles.summary: After the devastating Bhotekoshi flood on August 26, the family of Raj Kumar Shrestha performed funeral rites despite the victim’s body remaining missing. Relatives said a body that looked like Shrestha was photographed, but they could not locate it after being informed it had been transferred from Nuwakot to TU Teaching Hospital. The uncertainty over the body’s whereabouts has left the family in distress as they seek closure.

articles.title: Trade shifts to under-resourced Korala point after Rasuwa and Tatopani closures
articles.summary: Following the closure of the Rasuwa and Tatopani border points, traders are rerouting stranded containers to the under‑resourced Korala crossing in upper Mustang. Customs officials have warned that the Korala point lacks sufficient manpower and equipment to handle the sudden increase in trade flow, urging the government to allocate additional resources. The shift highlights vulnerabilities in Nepal’s trade infrastructure and could affect supply chains and revenue until the other crossings reopen.

articles.title: In Thecho, Matayaa becomes a festival of remembrance and satire
articles.summary: Thecho's annual Matayaa festival this year combined remembrance and satire, honoring those who lost their lives in the Bhotekoshi floods. The procession featured music, performances, and comedic commentary that reflected on societal issues while paying tribute to the flood victims, continuing the tradition of using art and humor to engage the community.

articles.title: US launches new strikes on Iran and Tehran hits back in widening conflict
articles.summary: The United States conducted airstrikes targeting Iranian military facilities, prompting Tehran to launch retaliatory attacks across the Gulf region. The escalating exchange has raised concerns of a broader conflict and the potential for renewed disruptions to global oil supplies, as shipping lanes and production hubs could be threatened. International observers warn that the tit‑for‑tat actions risk drawing in regional allies and could destabilize already fragile Middle‑East geopolitics.

articles.title: Rescue teams struggle to reach workers trapped in underground powerhouses
articles.summary: Rescue teams are facing severe difficulties reaching dozens of workers believed to be trapped inside underground hydropower plants after the Bhotekoshi flood swept through the area. Mud and debris have blocked access routes, delaying rescue operations. Families of the workers are demanding answers and urgent action from authorities. The incident highlights the vulnerability of Nepal's hydropower infrastructure to extreme weather events and the challenges of emergency response in remote mountainous regions.

articles.title: Sonu Sood arrives in Nepal with relief supplies for flood victims
articles.summary: Indian actor Sonu Sood arrived in Nepal carrying food and blankets supplied by his Sood Charity Foundation for communities affected by recent floods. The foundation aims to provide immediate relief and has pledged to continue assistance over the coming months, supporting flood‑hit districts across the country.
